sn12.51:3.1: Pali is rich in expressions for inner reflection and investigation. Sometimes this process is called “inner self-examination” ([sn12.66:3.3](), sometimes “rational application of mind” ([sn12.4:2.3]()).
sn12.51:9.1: This is one of the defining passages showing that the primary sense of _saṅkhāra_ here is “choices” either good, bad, or “imperturbable”. See also [mn57:9.2](), [an3.23](), [an4.233]().
sn12.51:9.3: The fourth absorption and above are called “imperturbable” (_āneñja_) because they are associated with equanimous feeling. This is technically distinguished from “good” or “meritorious” (_puñña_) choices, whose outcome is pleasant feeling.
